title: Understanding Codons
text: Remember that a codon is a sequence of $$3$$ DNA letters. Since each letter can be one of T, G, C, or A, think about how many different combinations of $$3$$ letters you can make.

title: Calculating Combinations
text: To find the number of possible codons, consider the number of choices you have for each position in the codon. Multiply these choices together to get the total number of combinations.

title: Number of Codons
text: How many different codons can be formed from the DNA letters T, G, C, and A?

title: One-Hot Encoding Codons
text: When one-hot encoding, each unique item gets its own dimension. If you have $$64$$ unique codons, how many dimensions will you need for one-hot encoding?

title: Dimensions for One-Hot Encoding
text: If each codon is represented by a unique dimension, and there are $$64$$ codons, how many dimensions will a single DNA string of $$3000$$ letters have when one-hot encoded by codons?
